Subject: Monthly KPI digest + QBR prep: action items on latency/cost signals

Folks — attaching the November KPI digest ahead of next week's QBR prep slot. High-level signals I want on the radar: 

- EU p99 latency +12% month-over-month (spiky, correlates with longer sequences on a small subset of routes).
- Hosted token cost per 1k up ~7% (model mix shift + bursty heavy-generation jobs).
- Uptime is 99.95% — within SLA but two transient node restarts on 10/28 in eu-west.
- Usage: embeddings up 34% driven by trial cohorts; this looks like a sustained new workload.

Asks: 
1) Laura — can you lead a short triage on the EU latency spike and produce a 1-page summary + recommended mitigation (pin vs throttle vs region routing) by EOD Wed? Attach runbook notes if you have them.
2) Marcus — please enumerate quick wins to reduce unit cost for hosted customers (quantization profiles, batching tweaks, routing). Prioritize items that can be in a canary for the QBR demo.
3) Evelyn — consolidate top 3 slides (latency, cost, usage) for the exec QBR deck; aim for one slide each and a single call-to-action.

Related attachments: 2026-11-redwood-kpi-dashboard.pdf (full dashboard), eu-latency-investigation-notes.md (raw logs + traces).

I copied Sarah from Acme because their renewal review is next week and they wanted to be kept in the loop on any customer-impacting trends.

Thanks — Logan

--
Logan Wright
VP, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Monthly KPI digest + QBR prep: action items on latency/cost signals

Logan — I dug into the EU p99 spike this morning. Summary (quick):

- Signal: p99 jump concentrated on /v1/chat/generate for r12 models between 10/25–10/29.
- Root cause candidate: a small set (~3%) of requests with long system prompts and high max_tokens; these bypassed prefix cache and triggered large KV cache churn on the GPU host.
- Evidence: tail traces show repeated KV cache invalidation and host-level GC events aligning with the spikes.

Recommended immediate mitigations:
- Temporary policy: route long-sequence (>1024 tokens) requests to dedicated capacity pool with larger KV budget (can be done with a routing rule TTL = 48 hours). Owner: laura_bennett.
- Prefix-cache heuristic: treat system-dominant prompts as cacheable after stable-run validation (needs infra work, mid-term).
- Telemetry: add a short-lived alert for sequence-length distribution crossing 95th pct for each region.

Attached: eu-latency-investigation-notes.md (raw trace snippets). I can produce the 1-pager by Wed EOD with recommended rollback plan and expected cost delta for the dedicated-route experiment.

Laura
Director, Inference Reliability
Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick follow-ups on cost side: 

- Immediate canaries (low-risk):
  * Per-route batching incentives: change batching window for non-chat routes for 24h to capture low-hanging wins (estimated -2.5% unit cost).
  * Auto-quantize suggestion: for internal A/B we can push q4 quantization recommendations for r9/recent models where quality delta < 1.2% on our evals.

- Medium runway: fast-path routing for high-volume embeddings to a quantized embedding pool. If we convert 40% of trial cohorts, we could knock embeddings cost -18% for that cohort.

I'll draft a short cost-impact table (3 rows) and upload it to the Drive folder; can present a one-slide cost play in the QBR. Owner: marcus_lin.
